posts.cooked:
https://greaterthangames.com/comment/58413#comment-58413

The last 3 posts on that page clarify that the Sentinels Set-up card is an in play card.

I had always assumed the Ennead set-up card was a villain card in play, like other set-up cards. Why is there a specific ruling for this one, if I may?
posts.raw:
https://greaterthangames.com/comment/58413#comment-58413

The last 3 posts on that page clarify that the Sentinels Set-up card is an in play card.

I had always assumed the Ennead set-up card was a villain card in play, like other set-up cards. Why is there a specific ruling for this one, if I may?

posts.name: MigrantP
posts.cooked:
Because if it is, there are weird interactions. Can Cedistic Dissonant destroy it? If it's a character card, does it deal damage? How does that even make sense?

We asked Christopher, and he said what is written there.

Most villain instructions cards do not exist in the digital version. They are just part of the main character card. But the Ennead don't have one, and that instructions card needs to be there for the player to read, so it must exist in some way in the UI.
